messages:
mira: Heads-up — noticed a sharp latency spike this morning when us-west-2-gpu-a pool hit ~95% active. Token accounting counters show we hadn't hit the hard tenant TPM caps, but queue depth climbed and 99p latencies doubled. Anyone seen coupling like this between token-based limits and queueing?

anil: yep, this is where effective capacity vs theoretical capacity diverges. If we let token refill math max out to raw capacity we leave zero headroom for scheduling/serialization jitter.

josh: do you have numbers from the incident? was burst credits empty?

mira: burst credits were partly used, but the bigger issue looked like sustained inflight KV-cache priming + long tail decode for a subset of requests. The token bucket allowed steady issuance -> requests pile up at the scheduler.

carol: TL;DR: we need an explicit safety margin in fleet->TPM accounting and a queued-admission backpressure threshold. Without it, the admission controller thinks there are tokens to serve but runtime queues them.

anil: propose we compute an "effective_tpm" per pool = floor(raw_capacity_tpm * (1 - safety_margin)) and use that for admission and forecasting. Example math we used in sim: 

```
# simplified
effective_tpm = floor(total_gpu_slots * tokens_per_min_per_gpu * (1 - safety_margin))
# admission uses effective_tpm; refill uses EWMA to avoid refill spikes
refill_rate = EWMA(effective_tpm / 60, alpha=0.2)  # tokens/sec smoothed
```

anil: with safety_margin 0.10 we saw queue length drop ~40% and 99p latency drop ~30% in the sim.

samir: what about tenant fairness? if we cap by effective_tpm some tenants may see lower throughput than their contractual share. We need a policy to gradually restore capacity when measured headroom returns.

josh: agree. my suggestion: two knobs — safety_margin (global, pool-level) and a dynamic recovery window. Policy: keep a moving window (5m) of utilization; allow temporary override if utilization < 70% for 3 consecutive windows.

carol: for regional constraints we should also add cross-region fallback thresholds. If primary region queue > X or latency beyond Y, route new requests to fallback region (if tenant permits). That reduces local saturation blast radius.

mira: cost note: safety margin reduces usable capacity so it increases unit cost. we should quantify margin vs SLO improvement to pick a default. simulation results: 5% margin -> minor SLO gain, 10% -> sweet spot, 15% -> more SLO gain but ~12% capacity loss.

anil: action items: I will run a sweep sim with margins [5,10,15,20] across three workload mixes (burst-heavy, steady-chatty, long-context decodes) and report micrometrics (queue depth, 95/99 latency, TPU/GPU utilization).

josh: I'll push an admission-controller change to use effective_tpm and EWMA refill in a feature flag (flag: adm/eff-tpm). PR will include telemetry counters: admitted_by_effective_tpm, queued_drain_time_ms.

carol: ops-bot can you schedule the sim job and link results here? ops-bot: scheduled job id run-2026-03-18-42 on sim-cluster, ETA 3h.

ops-bot: Job run-2026-03-18-42 submitted. Logs at https://internal-sim/jobs/run-2026-03-18-42 (restricted).

mira: thanks. also let's add a short blurb for customers explaining why we might temporarily lower advertised TPM (safety margin) — framing as improved 99p latency and fewer request failures during pool hotspots.

samir: +1. also suggest offering a configurable tenant-level margin to let high-priority customers buy back headroom.

josh: noting risks: if margin too conservative, we pay for extra capacity. we should default to 10% and revisit after sim.

anil: agreed. will share sim artifacts and a candidate default in ~4h.

mira: perfect — thanks everyone.
